prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE exceptionally polished desktop website design comp, 1536x1024 landscape: the first viewport of a page plus the beginning of the next section. A real web layout, edge to edge, no device frame, no browser chrome.

The attached reference images are screenshots of the SAME website's already-built homepage. Carry over exactly: the header (the script wordmark "Birdcar" at left in a forward-leaning connected brush script; at right the nav "How I work", "Selected work", "Writing" and a compact canary-yellow pill button "Book a free Walkthrough →" with ink text), the pale daylight ground #edf3f0, near-black ink #0b141a, the heavy, tight, confident grotesk (Mona Sans) for every heading and body line, white pill tags with soft shadows, canary yellow #f7c848 only on actions and things in motion, teal #5fb8bf only for a resolved state, and the premium matte isometric miniature render style (soft studio daylight, fine architectural-model detail, pale wood, matte stone, teal-cyan floor tiles, a small canary). Do NOT copy the reference's content: no homepage headline, no full office diorama, no logo strip, no model shelf.

This page is "The Walkthrough": the booking page for a free, pitch-free, roughly one-hour conversation with Nick (Birdcar), a systems engineer who builds tools for established service businesses. Within three business days of the conversation the visitor receives a written report they keep: what's happening, what I recommend, and where I'd start. The visitor's job on this page: understand the offer and book a time.

STRUCTURE, in reading order (a personal letter from Nick, with the report as its enclosure):
1. Header, about 80px, exactly as the reference.
2. First viewport: a single large white letter sheet (x 150 to 980, from y 120 bleeding past the bottom edge), flat, square to the page, lifted off the daylight ground by a soft ambient shadow. Inside the sheet, generous margins: headline about 56px, ink, two lines: "An hour on the work. A report you can use." Then letter paragraphs at about 20px, ink-soft, comfortable line length: "When you're the person keeping track of everything, it's hard to step back far enough to see what needs to change. So I start with the people doing the work, not with software." / "In a free Walkthrough, you spend about an hour showing me the work that's giving you trouble. Within three business days you get my recommendations in writing." / "The hour is about your work. If you want to talk about hiring me, you'll bring it up, not me." Then a typeset sign-off in the same grotesk (NOT script): "Nick Cannariato, Birdcar". Then the canary-yellow button "Book a free Walkthrough →" and a small muted line "About an hour. A written report within three business days. Free."
RIGHT margin (x 1030 to 1460, y 170 to 760): the letter's enclosure, a premium matte isometric miniature of a slim bound report booklet lying on the daylight ground, three divider tabs visible along its edge, each labeled by a white pill tag: "What's happening", "What I recommend", and "Where I'd start" (this last tag is canary yellow). A small canary perches on the booklet's top edge. One contact shadow.
3. Below the letter's lower edge, at the very bottom right, the beginning of the next section heading on the daylight ground: "Bring the problem. I'll bring the questions."

ART DIRECTION: one dominant move, the letter as the page; the enclosure is secondary and quiet. Personal, direct, premium, adult. Not cute, not a scrapbook, no paper texture, no handwriting fonts, no tape or pins. No purple, no gradient orbs, no robots, no AI imagery, no stock photos, no prices, no fake metrics, no testimonials. Preserve all quoted words exactly. Treat it as a finished, shippable website.
